label: nevus
caption_gt: H&E-stained section (100x) showing histopathological features suggestive of intramucosal nevi. The image displays the proliferation of nevus cells, characterized by cohesive islands of polygonal to oval epithelioid cells with focal melanin pigment production. Nests of nevus cells are separated by a hyalinised band beneath the stratified squamous surface epithelium. The nevus cells exhibit junctional separation and differentiation, without significant cellular atypia or dysplasia. The associated fibrous connective tissue contains dense bundles of collagen fibres. A yellow arrow points to Type A cells, which are large and round, without dendritic processes, located at the periphery adjacent to the epithelium with intense melanin accumulation. A blue arrow points to Type B cells, which are uniform, round to polygonal, found in deeper layers, and show decreased melanin deposition. Lesional cells are observed close to the excision borders.
